title: Rami bar Berabbi or Berukhi
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: In Sanhedrin 17b they said (wherever it says “the Neharbelaim teach”) that it is Rami bar Berabbi; the Arukh, entry נהר, Rashi on Beitzah 8b and Dikdukei Soferim read Rami bar Berukhi. And what is cited in Seder HaDorot, “bar Beruni” — the author of Maskil LeEitan writes that bar Beruni is not found anywhere; Hyman objects that he overlooked a small error in Seder HaDorot, proposing “bar Berukhi,” and explaining that the kaf was slightly erased, leaving a nun. Yuchasin cites bar Berekhyah.
In Sefer HaKeritot, Leshon Limmudim, gate 3, he wrote: “The Neharbelaim teach” — this is Rav Bivi bar Bizna.

notes.text: Maskil LeEitan is a book title, not a place. Hyman owns the proposed Berukhi correction, criticism and kaf-to-nun physical explanation; digital evidence does not prove that history. שכ״מ is read as wherever. Sefer HaKeritot is a work, not a tractate.

Davidson Sanhedrin 17b directly identifies Neharbelaim with Rami bar Berabbi. Exact Arukh, Rashi Beitzah, Dikdukei Soferim, Yuchasin and Sefer HaKeritot alternatives remain Hyman’s reports. His erased-kaf account is not demonstrated by the digital spelling.
